## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The production change in `app/report.py` is correct: an exact `lines[0] != "REPORT v1"` match rejects the `REPORT v0` and `REPORT v10` headers that the old `startswith` check let through. `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` covers the new check. One of the two added tests passes only because its input is missing the `END` line, so it never tests the header version.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:11 — tests — `test_rejects_legacy_header` builds `legacy` with `"v0".join("REPORT v1\nversion=v1".rsplit("v1", 1))`. That only replaces the last `v1`, so the input becomes `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`. The header is still `REPORT v1` and there is no `END` line, so `parse_report` returns `None` at the `lines[-1] != "END"` check on `app/report.py:3` and never reaches the version check. The comment on line 9 ("changing the fixture's version to v0") also doesn't match what the code does. Could you use a complete report with a legacy header, such as `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"`, or delete this test because line 15 already covers that case? — The test still passes if the `REPORT v1` check is removed or reverted to `startswith("REPORT ")`, so it can't catch the regression it is named for.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `app/report.py:5` now requires the whole header to match exactly, so prefix variants like `REPORT v10` or `REPORT v1 extra` are rejected. `tests/test_report.py:15` uses a complete, otherwise valid report, so that test fails if the version check is removed.
